text:
matt: FYI escalated from Acme - their private Redwood VPC in eu-west-1 started throwing TLS handshake failures to the private endpoint around 08:12 UTC. They see 502s from our LB and intermittent "handshake_failure" in client logs. Can eng-sre take a look?
sarah: on it. any customer repro steps or logs from their side?
matt: yes, they sent this: "curl -v https://redwood-private.acme.internal/api/health" -> TLS alert handshake_failure. Also seeing ICMP Destination Unreachable when they try to reach internal DNS names.
acme_netops: confirmed. We can still ping the public mgmt IP but private endpoints time out. Also noticed IKE rekeys around the same time in our edge logs.
jake: assigning. first suspicion: IPsec NAT-T/UDP4500 or ESP being blocked by their new firewall rules. priya can you pull BGP/peering state and any NAT translations from the gateway?
priya: grabbing. Also checking the private Route53 resolver config — customer mentioned DNS briefly. Could be split-horizon name resolving failing if requests aren't reaching the resolver.
priya: gateway show:
```
peer: acme-gw-01 state: established
ike-sa: 1 child-sas active, last_rekey: 2026-09-08T08:11:58Z
esp: packets in: 0, packets out: 120k
nat-t: enabled, udp4500-translated: 0
```
priya: esp counters look odd (in:0). that suggests traffic egressing our side but not being encapsulated/received back. also no NAT-T hits.
jake: can we get a tcpdump on the customer-facing interface? filter udp port 500 or 4500 and esp.
sarah: acme_netops can you run:
```
sudo tcpdump -n -i eth0 'udp port 500 or udp port 4500 or proto 50'
```
and paste first 30s output?
acme_netops: pasted snippet:
```
08:11:58.123456 IP 203.0.113.5.4500 > 198.51.100.10.4500: UDP, length 64
08:12:01.987654 IP 198.51.100.10.500 > 203.0.113.5.500: UDP, length 76
# then silence
```
acme_netops: after that we see no replies from 198.51.100.10 on UDP4500
jake: interesting — their gateway is sending NAT-T but our host not responding on 4500. check host-level iptables/egress allowlist.
priya: checking host egress policy: security group for private-gw-eu-west1 has outbound allow for TCP/443 and ephemeral ports only. UDP 500/4500 and IP protocol 50 (ESP) were accidentally omitted in the last policy rollout.
matt: that would cause ESP traffic to be dropped; explains esp in:0
sarah: cross-checking DNS question: customer said internal names resolve intermittently. when IPsec down, their queries to our VPC resolver (10.2.0.2) fail and fall back to public resolver, returning stale records. That explains "private name -> public IP" mismatch causing cert SNI mismatch.
jake: so multiple fail modes compounding: 1) egress policy removed UDP/ESP 2) DNS fallback causing clients to talk to wrong IP with different cert 3) LB returning 502 when backend health checks fail across the tunnel.
priya: quick mitigation: add outbound rules to allow UDP ports 500 and 4500 to peer range and allow IP protocol 50 (ESP) for the peering security group. also re-enable NAT-T translations.
priya: applied rule change at 08:29 UTC. Can Acme confirm connectivity?
acme_netops: running tcpdump again -> we now see responses on 4500 and ESP traffic. IKE and child SA re-established at 08:30:02
acme_netops: curl health now returns 200 and TLS handshake is successful. thanks.
matt: passing update to account team.
sarah: follow-up - why did policy change? audit shows a config push at 07:58 UTC from infra-automation that tightened egress to "managed-only". someone omitted peering-needed UDP/ESP exception.
jake: action items:
- infra-automation: add peering exception template so UDP/ESP and peer IP ranges are exempt from managed-only rule (PR opened)
- docs: add runbook for Private peering connectivity (DNS fallback symptoms, tcpdump checks, ike/esp counters) (sarah)
- ops: check other customer peering SGs for same rollout impact (priya)
sarah: jotting down repro steps we used:
```
# verify IKE/ESP counters on our gateway
show ike-sa | grep -i established
show esp counters
# on customer side tcpdump
sudo tcpdump -n -i eth0 'udp port 500 or udp port 4500 or proto 50'
# check resolver reachability
dig @10.2.0.2 redwood-private.acme.internal +short
```
jake: adding postmortem note: root cause = infra-automation policy roll that removed peering exceptions; resulting in blocked UDP4500/ESP and dropped IKE child SAs; secondary impact = DNS fallback to public names causing TLS cert mismatch and 502s. Severity: P2. ETA for automation fix -> 2d for deploy + sync checks.
priya: scanning other SGs: found 3 other private peering SGs missing UDP/ESP; opened tickets and applied temporary allowlists where customers reported outages.
matt: acme is back to healthy. customer requested a short note summarizing cause and preventative steps; I'll send once we have the PR link and runbook.
jake: adding label :white_check_mark: marked resolved at 08:31 UTC. will include timeline in postmortem.
